# Document the Failure Mode Next to the Fix

Almost every note in these two repositories has the same shape: **state the wrong-but-plausible
alternative, name the concrete input that breaks it, then give the fix.** Not "we use a regex" but
"`split()` shifts every field after the first quoted one, silently".

> "Not hypothetical -- the sample log in data/ contains an injection attempt whose referer embeds \"
> sequences, and a naive [^\"]* would terminate the field at the first inner quote and reject the
> whole line."
> — Python-Programming-Laboratories/src/weblog/entry.py, 2026-07-25

> "**An assertion has to reach the code under test.** A test whose argument is an undefined name
> raises `NameError` while evaluating the call, before the function is entered — so
> `pytest.raises(TypeError)` never sees it, and the test would pass against an implementation doing no
> type checking at all."
> — Python-Programming-Laboratories/labs/07_testing/README.md, 2026-07-25

## Why this form and not a comment saying what the code does

The failure mode is the expensive knowledge. The fix is usually one line and re-derivable from the
code; *why the obvious thing is wrong* is not, and it is exactly what a reader is about to redo.
A note that says "parse with a regex" prevents nothing. A note that names the input that defeats
`split()` prevents the rewrite.

## The catalogue

- Quoted-field parsing and the injection-attempt referer — [[common-log-format-parsing]].
- The test that passed before entering the function; the `"no"`-is-truthy fixture trap —
  [[tests-that-pass-for-the-wrong-reason]].
- `Image.ANTIALIAS` and `ImageDraw.textsize` removed in Pillow 10, `findAll(text=True)` removed in
  BeautifulSoup 4.13 — [[pillow]] and [[beautifulsoup]].
- The Babel CDN leaving a blank page on `file://` — [[vendor-react-over-babel-cdn]].
- `errors="replace"` costing one skipped line rather than the run; `image_ratio` returning `None`
  "rather than print a zero"; `size=0` "so that summing it never needs a guard".

## Where it comes from

It is the load-bearing compensation for [[import-finished-work-into-git]]. In
[[python-programming-laboratories]] all twelve commits landed in one day with no fix commits at all —
so the Pillow port, the bs4 port, the restructured faculty site and the wrong-reason test exist
**only** as README prose. Where the git history is thin, the prose has to carry the diagnosis.

[[discrete-mathematics-laboratories]] does both: `48ba16d Fix UnicodeEncodeError in the lab3 demos on
Windows consoles` is a real corrective commit, *and* the lab-5 README writes out the CDN failure in
full. This is the sibling of [[provenance-and-limits-stated-inline]] — that pattern states what a
claim does not cover, this one states what a design already survived.
